name: Rutersju Hook
summary: A trick-taking game played with a 36-card pack. In each deal players bid 0-3 tricks in turn, and the last bidder may not make the bids total exactly 3. Players then play 3 tricks with simultaneous card choices and score for hitting their bid exactly.

player.meaning: Running point total. It may go negative.
Cards held this deal, each written 'strength:card', for example '36:♦7'.
Card played in the current trick. It is revealed only after all cards are chosen.
Whether this player is the declarer of the current deal.

game.meaning: The undealt cards. They stay hidden all deal.
Cards played face up so far this deal.
Length of the game: 3 deals per player.
The seat that bids last in this deal.
Sum of the bids made so far this deal.
Seat of the declarer; 0 means no declarer.

setup: Seats are numbered 1 to N, where N is 3, 4 or 5.
Every player's score is set to 0.
total_deals is set to 3 * N, priority_seat to 1 and deal_number to 0.

round.effect: Start a deal. Refill deck with all 36 cards. Clear every hand and played_cards. Set every bid, tricks and played to 0 or empty, every is_declarer to false, and bid_sum, declarer_seat and trick_number to 0. Deal 3 cards to each player: each card is a random draw removed from deck and appended to that player's hand.
Each player sees only their own hand.

round.who: each player in turn, starting with seat (priority_seat mod N) + 1, going up the seat numbers with wraparound, and ending with priority_seat
round.answer: A whole number from 0 to 3. For priority_seat, if bid_sum <= 3, the value 3 - bid_sum is not offered.
round.effect: The player's bid is set to the answer and bid_sum is increased by the answer. Each bidder hears all earlier bids.

If max bid is 0, set declarer_seat to 0. Otherwise declarer_seat is the seat with the highest bid; among tied players it is the one who bid latest in this deal's bidding order. Set is_declarer to true for that seat.
Announce every bid and the declarer (or 'no declarer').
Repeat the next three steps until trick_number = 3.

round.answer: One card from the player's own hand.
round.effect: Each player's played is set to the chosen card. No player sees any choice until all choices are in.
Remove each played card from its hand and append it to played_cards. The player whose played card has the highest strength (the number before the colon) adds 1 to tricks. Increase trick_number by 1.
Reveal all played cards together and announce the trick winner.

Settle the deal. For each player, let d = |bid - tricks|. If d = 0, score += 3 + bid; otherwise score -= 2 * d. In addition, if is_declarer is true: if d = 0, score += 1; otherwise score -= 1. Then deal_number += 1 and priority_seat = (priority_seat mod N) + 1.
Announce all bids, trick counts and scores, and the new priority_seat.
End the game if deal_number >= total_deals; otherwise start the next deal.

ending.decided_by: After 3N deals, the player with the highest score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, they share the result, which is the source's draw.

rules.text: When the game starts, every player has 0 points, priority_seat is 1, and total_deals is 3 * N (9 for 3 players, 12 for 4, 15 for 5).
When a deal starts, the full 36-card pack is reshuffled and each player is dealt exactly 3 cards into their hand, removed from deck. With N players, 36 - 3N cards stay hidden in deck.
When a hand is dealt, only its owner can see it, and deck is visible to no one.
When bidding happens, seats bid in order starting at the seat after priority_seat (wrapping from N to 1), each hearing all earlier bids, and priority_seat bids last.
When any player bids, the bid is a whole number from 0 to 3.
When the priority seat bids and the others' bids sum to s <= 3, the bid 3 - s is not allowed. For example, if the others sum to 1, the priority seat may bid 0, 1 or 3 but not 2.
When the others' bids sum to more than 3, the priority seat may bid any of 0, 1, 2 or 3.
When bidding ends, the player with the highest bid is the declarer. If players tie for the highest bid, the tied player who bid latest is the declarer.
When every bid is 0, there is no declarer (declarer_seat = 0).
When a trick is played, every player simultaneously chooses one card from their hand, and no choice is seen until all are in.

When the cards of a trick are revealed, the card with the highest strength wins, with no need to follow suit, and its player's tricks increases by 1. For example, ♦7 (36) beats ♦A (35), and ♦6 (28) beats ♠A (27).
When a card is played, it leaves the hand and is added to the public played_cards list.
When a deal has had 3 tricks, it moves to settlement.
When a player's tricks equals their bid, they gain 3 + bid points: 3 for bid 0, 4 for bid 1, 5 for bid 2, 6 for bid 3.
When a player's tricks differ from their bid by d > 0, they lose 2 * d points. For example, bid 3 with 1 trick loses 4.
When the declarer hits their bid exactly, they gain 1 extra point. When the declarer misses, they lose 1 extra point.
When settlement ends, scores may be negative, deal_number increases by 1, and priority_seat moves to (priority_seat mod N) + 1.
When deal_number reaches 3 * N, the game ends and the player with the highest score wins. A tie at the top is a draw, shared among the tied players.

offers.question: Bid
offers.options: If the sum s of the earlier bids is <= 3: 0, 1, 2, 3 except 3 - s. If s > 3: 0, 1, 2, 3.

offers.question: Card for the trick
offers.options: Exactly the cards currently in that player's own hand (3 in trick 1, 2 in trick 2, 1 in trick 3).

choices.why: The designer suggests 4, so it is kept. 3 is the smallest table where the hook and declarer contests bite. Above 5, 3 tricks spread over too many players, so most bids are 0 and one choice matters little.

choices.what: 'Left' means the next higher seat number, wrapping from N to 1
choices.why: The engine has no physical table, and seat order must be concrete.

choices.what: Cards are written as 'strength:card', for example '36:♦7'
choices.why: The engine has no lookup table, so putting the strength in the card text lets the trick winner be found by comparing numbers.
The rules forbid discussion; players communicate only through bids and cards.

choices.what: Bidding uses ask; card play uses poll
choices.why: Bids are made in turn and each bidder hears earlier bids, while cards are chosen secretly and simultaneously.

simplifications.what: A tie for the highest score is shown as a shared win among the tied players
simplifications.why: The engine ranks by one expression and players level at the top share the win. This is equivalent to the source's draw.

simplifications.what: Scratch value d = |bid - tricks| is computed inside the settlement step rather than stored
simplifications.why: The rules never refer to it outside settlement.
